parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks tier-1 universal exposures: a national entry regime barring marker self-selection and directing visa refusal on any sex discrepancy (possible lifetime fraud finding), documented trans travellers stranded with blocked passports, and eight-plus foreign governments issuing advisories after detentions. The division adds birth-certificate bathroom mandates, a binary-sex statute, a college ban, surgery-requirement ID rules upheld by a hostile circuit, no statewide nondiscrimination or GI hate-crime coverage, and a 10-year provider felony for under-19 transition care that reaches a travelling family. Federal custody carries documented conversion-therapy and abuse practices. No criminalisation of identity itself, some EOs enjoined, national employment/hate-crime protections, and no usable trans-violence rate keep this out of the 0.15-0.25 tiers, but documented universal exposures without working remedy place it in Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order defines binary sex; X markers and non-assigned-sex markers stopped Feb 2025; cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and stranded abroad; neighbouring citizens detained over visa issues; multiple foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; the marker policy remains litigated by a civil-liberties union; a legal-aid FAQ advises on documentation strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor's home passport is still screened under the cable; discrepancy can mean refusal, secondary screening, or a fraud referral that ends future travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (haircut, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs) from 2026; transgender immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; a trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward under a sister unit's bathroom law.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several related executive orders are blocked or enjoined; litigation pending.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A routine state stop, ID check or facility ejection can escalate into federal custody where birth-sex placement and care withdrawal apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: HB322 requires school bathrooms by birth-certificate gender; a July 2026 assessment records a college-campus bathroom ban (bill text unverified); SB 79 (Feb 2025) declares immutable binary sex and permits sex-segregated spaces by biology. Nationally 22 units have facility bans, 4 criminalising in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No documented criminal trespass provision for this division specifically; private settings largely unaffected here; map shows 29 units without mapped bans.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Handcuff arrest under a comparable unit's restroom law shows the escalation pathway; outed visitors in public buildings carry continuous exclusion risk.

care_services.exposure: Class C felony, 10 years, for providers giving puberty blockers, hormones or surgery to under-19s, enforceable since Aug 2023 and unchallenged since May 2025; no statewide nondiscrimination, no ban on insurance exclusions, no inclusive state-employee benefits.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitors; national employment healthcare nondiscrimination exists but is resident-sphere climate only.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces provider-refusal, no insurance recourse, and possible state inquiry if care is sought.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises identifying and neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 DOJ rewards memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; January 2025 order calls gender-affirming care 'mulctilation' and directs investigation of schools; another order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition; genocide-stage comparisons by advocates.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The memo states ideology is never a reward criterion and counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises severity of any police, school or border encounter for an outed visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Provider felony for under-19 care; school bathroom mandates; order directing criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; proposed Oct 2025 rule barring public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care; DOJ subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for under-19 patient records.
minors_guardians.protection: Several national orders blocked or enjoined; the parent is not the defendant under the provider felony; proposals unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling guardian with a trans minor can be met with care denial, missed schooling, record scrutiny or state inquiry.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law (1994) excludes gender identity; no statewide employment, housing or public-accommodations protection; only two municipalities fully protect; polling ranks the division among lowest-support for trans-inclusive policy.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and 2020 employment nondiscrimination ruling apply; circuit applies gender identity to sex in employment law since 2011.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An assaulted visitor has thin local recourse and would depend on federal mechanisms with limited reach during a short stay.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide public-accommodations recourse; this circuit reversed surgery-requirement invalidation (Corbitt) and upheld licence refusal Sept-Dec 2024, so document remedies fail locally; pending national challenges make exposure time-dependent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple executive orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ; national employment and hate-crime protections; three cities cover public employment.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are city-by-city and slow; a short-stay visitor is unlikely to obtain relief before departure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Saruth routinely detains trans visitors in crowded cells after secondary inspection with capital decrees in the background and illusory habeas. Here entry exposure is refusal, secondary screening and possible lifetime ineligibility, not routine cell detention; custody abuse is documented but post-arrest, not the default entry pathway. Safer than 0.15-B.

Ostravia has birth-sex prison placement and cross-dressing arrests in administrative buildings with slow remedies. Our dossier shares facility exclusion and document friction, but adds a nationwide hostile apparatus (entry refusal, counterterrorism framing, custody conversion practices, provider felony) and a hostile circuit on documents — more layered exposure than 0.25-C, yet no routine fining or raid pattern here, so above it.

Drellia's mandatory registration, nightly hotel transmission and repeated interviews create durable ID exposure with rare imprisonment and a slow ombudsman. Comparable here: continuous document/facility exposure, no credible imprisonment for identity itself, weak remedies. Our dossier is somewhat worse (entry fraud referral, care felony for minors, custody abuses, hostile courts), so slightly below 0.45-D.

Meridia accepts marker-congruent passports, trains border officers, and offers a tribunal with counsel and compensation for brief detention. Here the entry regime bars marker self-selection and directs refusal on discrepancy, with no equivalent trained-officer or tribunal protection. Well below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one continuous national entry exposure (marker regime, discrepancy-triggered refusal, possible fraud finding) fused with division-level facility exclusion, birth-certificate ID rules upheld by a hostile circuit, no statewide recourse, and a provider felony that converts a travelling family's care-seeking into a legal hazard. Federal custody practices supply the severity ceiling: conversion-therapy mandates and documented abuse in immigration detention. Offsetting these are real but partial: no criminalisation of trans identity itself, several orders enjoined, national employment and hate-crime protections, an existing-valid-X-passport window, and a violence figure that is an unusable undercount floor rather than evidence of a campaign. Recourse exists on paper yet is shown failing in this circuit, so documented universal exposures dominate. The result sits in Elevated Risk: materially safer than routine-detention jurisdictions, materially worse than jurisdictions where markers are accepted and remedies work.
